judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's mathematical claims hold under independent recomputation: 4(x+7)=4x+28; 3(4+5)=27 against Kim's 3(4)+5=17; 5(2)+3(3)=19 against Devon's 8(2)(3)=48; 7a+4-2a+9=5a+13; 8-2(1-3)=12 against Nadia's 0; 5(2x-3)+4x=14x-15; 6x+15=3(2x+5); and 3(2*3-4)-2(3-5)=6+4=10 against the classmate's 6x-12-2x-10 = -10 at x=3. Its manual_items_reviewed 1 also matches verify.json, which correctly splits problem 8 into a manual entry for part (a) and an eval entry for part (b). But the judge scored answer_key_quality 4 without reading the bank the key prints: Quick Answers row 7 reads "7. 6x + 15" for the problem that asks the student to FACTOR 6x + 15. The verified expected is "3*(2*x+5)", and _fmt's bare sympify auto-expands it back into the question — I confirmed that sympy.latex(sympy.sympify('3*(2*x+5)')) returns '6 x + 15'. A grader scanning the bank sees the problem statement where the answer should be, while the worked solution on page 2 boxes the correct 3(2x + 5). Separately, problems 2 and 3 both end "say in a few words which term Kim forgot to multiply" and "why 5x and 3y cannot be pulled into one term" and carry eval entries only — the same open-response demand problem 8(a) handles correctly.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 8 is the correct pattern for a mixed item and should be the template for the rest of the suite: verify.json declares BOTH a {"type": "manual"} entry for part (a) carrying the full-credit criteria (a letter stands for an unknown, unlike terms count different things, one substitution that disagrees) and an eval entry expecting 10 for part (b).

All four planted wrong answers are declared as traps whose expr is the wrong METHOD (3*x + 5, 8*x*y, 8 - 2*x - 6, 6*x - 12 - 2*x - 10), not a hand-typed number, so verify.py proved each one is both reachable by the misconception and rejected by the problem's own check.

The key gives each error a size rather than a label: Kim's gap of 27-17=10 is exactly the 15-5 she never multiplied, and Nadia's 12 is the whole amount lost to the sign. That is a diagnosis a parent can act on.

The substitution values were chosen so the wrong and right versions actually disagree — final_response.md notes that at x=0 Nadia's error would have been invisible, which is the kind of design decision worth keeping.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers._fmt calls sympy.sympify with evaluation on, so any expected written in a requested FORM (factored, unexpanded) is normalised to sympy's canonical form before being typeset into the delivered key.
evidence: answer_key.pdf Quick Answers: "7. 6x + 15" — the question restated.
answer_key.pdf page 2 problem 7 correctly boxes 3(2x + 5), so only the generated bank is wrong.

root_causes.description: The contract has no rule requiring a manual entry when a stem asks the student to NAME the error in words, so an error-analysis sheet whose whole focus is diagnosis records the diagnoses as unverified prose.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 2: "then say in a few words which term Kim forgot to multiply" — verify.json id 2 is an eval on 3*(x+5) only.
worksheet.pdf problem 3: "then say in a few words why 5x and 3y cannot be pulled into one term" — verify.json id 3 is an eval only.
verify.json id 8 shows the author already knows the two-entry pattern, so the omission is inconsistency rather than ignorance.

improvements.title: Preserve the authored form of factor/unexpanded expecteds in the Quick Answers bank
improvements.proposed_change: In render_quick_answers._fmt, stop normalising form-bearing expecteds. Parse the string with evaluate=False (or wrap the parsed result in sympy.UnevaluatedExpr, or re-apply sympy.factor for entries whose problem type is "factor") so the bank typesets the form the problem asked for. The renderer already knows each entry's type via by_id, so the branch can be keyed on it rather than guessed from the string.
improvements.regression_test: Extend tests/test_render_quick_answers.py with a verify JSON holding {"id": 1, "type": "factor", "expr": "6*x + 15", "expected": "3*(2*x+5)"} and assert the rendered bank line contains a factor times a bracket (e.g. "3 \\left(2 x + 5\\right)") and does NOT contain "6 x + 15". The assertion fails on today's renderer.
improvements.expected_impact: Factoring, completing-the-square, interval and any other form-graded problem regains a usable bank entry across the suite; on this sheet row 7 stops printing the question as its own answer.
improvements.risk: evaluate=False parsing changes the printed shape of every string expected, so the whole quick-answer fixture set has to be re-baselined; entries authored in a deliberately unsimplified form ("24/36") would start printing unsimplified unless the branch is restricted to form-bearing types.

improvements.title: Fail the build when a problem stem asks for reasoning and its verify entry is machine-only
improvements.proposed_change: Add a delivery-blocking lint that pairs the worksheet source with the verify JSON: scan each \problem block for an open-response demand ("explain", "say why", "say how you decided", "in one sentence", "what went wrong", "find her mistake", "describe", "sketch", "plot", "graph it") and fail the build when that problem id carries no {"type": "manual"} entry. SKILL.md should state the rule positively: a problem that asks for a value AND a sentence gets TWO verify entries, the machine one for the value and a manual one carrying the full-credit criteria, exactly as this run already does elsewhere.
improvements.regression_test: New fixture pair under tests/fixtures: a worksheet .tex whose problem 3 stem ends "Explain in one sentence why ..." beside a verify.json whose id 3 holds only an eval entry. tests/check_prose_consistency.py must exit non-zero naming problem 3; adding {"id": 3, "type": "manual", "desc": ...} makes it exit 0. The test fails today because no checker reads the stem for open-response prose.
improvements.expected_impact: The gate chain's manual-flag count starts telling the truth, so a grader is told which written answers nobody machine-checked instead of reading "nothing is flagged for manual review" under a sheet full of explanation prompts. On curr-174 the manual count moves from 1 to 3, picking up the "name the error" halves of problems 2 and 3 that are the declared focus of the sheet.
improvements.risk: Keyword matching will flag stems whose imperative is decorative ("show your work"), so the lint needs a curated phrase list and an explicit per-problem opt-out, or authors will start declaring hollow manual entries to silence it.

case_summary: A strong misconception sheet on invalid distribution and unlike-term combination. Three explicit find-and-fix items (Kim, Devon, Nadia) exceed the prompt's minimum of two, every planted wrong result is a machine-checked trap derived from the wrong method rather than a typed number, and the substitution test is used consistently as the tool that settles equivalence. I recomputed all eight answers and all four trap values and found no mathematical error. One delivery defect: the generated Quick Answers bank prints "6x + 15" for problem 7, whose verified answer is the factored 3(2x + 5), because _fmt's sympify expands it — the bank restates the question. Problems 2 and 3 also require a written naming of the error with no manual entry, though problem 8 shows the author already knows the correct two-entry pattern.
